titleStmt.title: A survey on Image Data Augmentation for Deep Learning
titleStmt.author: Connor Shorten
Taghi M. Khoshgoftaar

publicationStmt.p: Tag layer of the DHSS Meta-Tagging Project. The article text is reproduced from the staged copy named in sourceDesc and is not altered; the tags are held separately in standOff so that overlapping and nested spans are preserved.

bibl.title: A survey on Image Data Augmentation for Deep Learning

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: image Data Augmentation techniques, from geometric transforms to GANs, as a remedy for overfitting on limited data
span.quote: Data Augmentation encompasses a suite of techniques that enhance the size and quality of training datasets such that better Deep Learning models can be built using them.

span.label: what to do about overfitting when the application domain has no big data to be had
span.quote: In contrast to the techniques mentioned above, Data Augmentation approaches overfitting from the root of the problem, the training dataset.

span.label: a taxonomy of image augmentation split into data warping and oversampling, together with the statement that the split is not exclusive
span.quote: Oversampling and Data Warping augmentations do not form a mutually exclusive dichotomy. For example, GAN samples can be stacked with random cropping to further inflate the dataset.

span.label: method
span.quote: Data Augmentation encompasses a suite of techniques that enhance the size and quality of training datasets such that better Deep Learning models can be built using them.

span.label: overfitting - a model learning a function of very high variance that models its training data perfectly
span.quote: Overfitting refers to the phenomenon when a network learns a function with very high variance such as to perfectly model the training data.

span.label: a survey organised by where the augmentation intervenes, with medical imaging as the motivating limited-data case
span.term: a survey organised by where the augmentation intervenes, with medical imaging as the motivating limited-data case
span.quote: Limited datasets is an especially prevalent challenge in medical image analysis.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: AUGMENTATION IS AN ASSUMPTION, AND THE PAPER STATES IT: that more information can be extracted from the dataset already held. Everything else follows from whether that is true of a given dataset
span.quote: This is done under the assumption that more information can be extracted from the original dataset through augmentations.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: WHAT AUGMENTATION IS ACTUALLY TEACHING: the invariances a recogniser must survive - viewpoint, lighting, occlusion, background, scale - are baked into the DATA rather than into the architecture
span.quote: The task of Data Augmentation is to bake these translational invariances into the dataset such that the resulting models will perform well despite these challenges.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: SIMULATING BIG DATA RATHER THAN OBTAINING IT: overfitting is not much of a problem when data is abundant, so augmentation gives a limited dataset the characteristics of an abundant one
span.quote: Overfitting is generally not as much of an issue with access to big data. Data Augmentation prevents overfitting by modifying limited datasets to possess the characteristics of big data.

span.label: an unsafe transformation could be made useful rather than harmful by softening the label, so the model learns uncertainty instead of a falsehood - but building those labels is too costly
span.quote: A non-label preserving transformation could potentially strengthen the model’s ability to output a response indicating that it is not confident about its prediction.

span.label: oversampling works by re-balancing the class distribution so the model is not biased toward answering with the majority class
span.quote: Oversampling is a technique used to re-sample imbalanced class distributions such that the model is not overly biased towards labeling instances as the majority class type.

span.label: medical imaging is short of data FOR STRUCTURAL REASONS, and the paper names rarity first: `It is especially difficult to build big medical image datasets DUE TO THE RARITY OF DISEASES`. The remaining three reasons it lists - patient privacy, the need for expert labellers, and the cost of the scans - are separated from this clause by a journal running header in the staged text and are not inside this span.
span.quote: It is especially difficult to build big medical image datasets due to the rarity of diseases

span.label: rotation safety is set by one parameter: small rotations help digit recognition and large ones destroy the label, so the same transform is safe and unsafe at different magnitudes
span.quote: The safety of rotation augmentations is heavily determined by the rotation degree parameter.

span.label: cropping and translation differ in what they preserve - cropping shrinks the input, translation keeps the spatial dimensions and pads the vacated space
span.quote: The contrast between random cropping and translations is that cropping will reduce the size of the input such as (256,256) → (224, 224), whereas translations preserve the spatial dimensions of the image.

span.label: colour transformations trade colour bias for spatial characteristics, which is a gain only where colour is not the distinguishing feature
span.quote: In effect, color space transformations will eliminate color biases present in the dataset in favor of spatial characteristics.

span.label: a kernel filter can be rebuilt as a convolution layer with the right padding and activation, so the augmentation duplicates what the network already does
span.quote: For example, something like PatchShuffle Regularization could be implemented with a convolution layer.

span.label: AUGMENTATION CANNOT CREATE A CLASS THAT IS ABSENT: no method surveyed will produce a golden retriever from a dataset of bulldogs. It can lessen biases of lighting, occlusion, scale and background, and it cannot supply missing content
span.quote: no augmentation method discussed, from SamplePairing to AutoAugment to GANs, will create a golden retriever.

span.label: The stated bias limit in the paper's own words, which bounds every technique it surveys
span.quote: Data Augmentation cannot overcome all biases present in a small dataset.

span.label: The survey covers IMAGE data only, with transfer to other data domains asserted rather than shown
span.quote: This survey focuses on applications for image data, although many of these techniques and concepts can be expanded to other data domains.

span.label: The taxonomy the survey is organised by does not partition its own subject - warping and oversampling are stated not to be mutually exclusive
span.quote: Oversampling and Data Warping augmentations do not form a mutually exclusive dichotomy. For example, GAN samples can be stacked with random cropping to further inflate the dataset.

span.label: safety is domain-dependent, which is precisely what makes a generalisable augmentation policy hard
span.quote: This is somewhat domain dependent, providing a challenge for developing generalizable augmentation policies, (see Auto- Augment [38] for further exploration into finding generalizable augmentations).

span.label: there is NO image processing function that cannot flip a label at some distortion magnitude - the strongest form of the claim, stated by the authors
span.quote: There is no image processing function that cannot result in a label changing transformation at some distortion magnitude.

span.label: constructing refined labels for every unsafe augmentation is computationally expensive, which is why the cheap option is to avoid unsafe transforms
span.quote: However, constructing refined labels for every non-safe Data Augmentation is a computationally expensive process.

span.label: many experiments deliberately restrict themselves to a subset of a large dataset in order to SIMULATE a limited-data problem rather than face a real one
span.quote: Many experiments constrain themselves to a subset of the dataset to simulate limited data problems.

span.label: kernel filters are very close to the internal mechanism of a CNN, which is the argument for making them a layer rather than a dataset operation
span.quote: A disadvantage of this technique is that it is very similar to the internal mechanisms of CNNs.

span.label: in medical imaging the gap between training and test data is more complex than position and translation, so geometric transformations have limited scope there
span.quote: Finally, in many of the application domains covered such as medical image analysis, the biases distancing the training data from the testing data are more complex than positional and translational variances.

span.label: colour transformations can discard the information the task depends on - darkening may hide the object entirely
span.quote: Additionally, color transformations may discard important color information and thus are not always a label-preserving transformation.

span.label: transformations that may alter the label, such as translation or random cropping, must be checked by hand
span.quote: Some geometric transformations such as translation or random cropping must be manually observed to make sure they have not altered the label of the image.

span.label: SMOTE and Borderline-SMOTE were built to interpolate new points for imbalanced TABULAR data and are carried over to images
span.quote: SMOTE and the extension of Borderline-SMOTE [30] create new instances by interpolating new points from existing instances via k-Nearest Neighbors.

span.label: transfer learning is explained by the anecdote that a pianist learns guitar faster, and augmentation by analogy with imagination and dreaming
span.quote: For example, a human intelligence anecdote of transfer learning is illustrated in learning music.

span.label: Data Augmentation
span.quote: Data Augmentation encompasses a suite of techniques that enhance the size and quality of training datasets such that better Deep Learning models can be built using them.

span.label: Generalizability
span.quote: Generalizability refers to the performance difference of a model when evaluated on previously seen data (training data) versus data it has never seen before (testing data).

span.label: overfitting
span.quote: In contrast to the techniques mentioned above, Data Augmentation approaches overfitting from the root of the problem, the training dataset.

span.label: data warping
span.quote: Data warping augmentations transform existing images such that their label is preserved. This encompasses augmentations such as geometric and color transformations, random erasing, adversarial training, and neural style transfer. Oversampling augmentations create synthetic instances and add them to the training set. This includes mixing images, feature space augmentations, and generative adversarial networks (GANs).

span.label: oversampling
span.quote: Data warping augmentations transform existing images such that their label is preserved. This encompasses augmentations such as geometric and color transformations, random erasing, adversarial training, and neural style transfer. Oversampling augmentations create synthetic instances and add them to the training set. This includes mixing images, feature space augmentations, and generative adversarial networks (GANs).

span.label: Dropout
span.quote: Dropout [7] is a regularization technique that zeros out the activation values of randomly chosen neurons during training. This constraint forces the network to learn more robust features rather than relying on the predictive capability of a small subset of neurons in the network.

span.label: Batch normalization
span.quote: Batch normalization [9] is another regularization technique that normalizes the set of activations in a layer. Normalization works by subtracting the batch mean from each activation and dividing by the batch standard deviation.

span.label: Transfer Learning
span.quote: This differs from Transfer Learning because in Transfer Learning, the network architecture such as VGG-16 [2] or ResNet [3] must be transferred as well as the weights.

span.label: Pretraining
span.quote: In Pretraining, the network architecture is defined and then trained on a big dataset such as ImageNet [12]. This differs from Transfer Learning because in Transfer Learning, the network architecture such as VGG-16 [2] or ResNet [3] must be transferred as well as the weights.

span.label: translational invariances
span.quote: The task of Data Augmentation is to bake these translational invariances into the dataset such that the resulting models will perform well despite these challenges.

span.label: training dataset
span.quote: In contrast to the techniques mentioned above, Data Augmentation approaches overfitting from the root of the problem, the training dataset.

span.label: regularization technique
span.quote: Dropout [7] is a regularization technique that zeros out the activation values of randomly chosen neurons during training. This constraint forces the network to learn more robust features rather than relying on the predictive capability of a small subset of neurons in the network.

span.label: big data
span.quote: Overfitting is generally not as much of an issue with access to big data. Data Augmentation prevents overfitting by modifying limited datasets to possess the characteristics of big data.

span.label: GAN samples
span.quote: Oversampling and Data Warping augmentations do not form a mutually exclusive dichotomy. For example, GAN samples can be stacked with random cropping to further inflate the dataset.

span.label: safety
span.quote: The safety of a Data Augmentation method refers to its likelihood of preserving the label post-transformation.

span.label: class imbalance
span.quote: Class imbalance describes a dataset with a skewed ratio of majority to minority samples.

span.label: Random Oversampling
span.quote: Random Oversampling (ROS) is a naive approach which duplicates images randomly

span.label: SMOTE
span.quote: Intelligent oversampling techniques date back to SMOTE (Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique), which was developed by Chawla et al. [29].

span.label: refined labels
span.quote: If the label of the image after a non-label preserving transformation is something like [0.5 0.5], the model could learn more robust confidence predictions.

span.label: Neural Style Transfer
span.quote: Data Augmentation methods such as GANs and Neural Style Transfer can ‘imagine’ alterations to images such that they have a better understanding of them.

span.label: positional bias
span.quote: Shifting images left, right, up, or down can be a very useful transformation to avoid positional bias in the data.

span.label: kernel filters
span.quote: Kernel filters are a very popular technique in image processing to sharpen and blur images.

span.label: PatchShuffle
span.quote: Kang et al. [64] experiment with a unique kernel filter that randomly swaps the pixel values in an n × n sliding window.

span.label: color space transformations
span.quote: Therefore, the effectiveness of color space transformations, also known as photometric transformations, is fairly intuitive to conceptualize.

span.label: noise injection
span.quote: Noise injection consists of injecting a matrix of random values usually drawn from a Gaussian distribution.

span.label: Data Augmentation - A DATA-SPACE SOLUTION, defined by WHERE it intervenes rather than by what it does: every other remedy for overfitting changes the model, and this one changes the dataset
span.quote: In contrast to the techniques mentioned above, Data Augmentation approaches overfitting from the root of the problem, the training dataset.

span.label: data warping - the label is PRESERVED and an existing image is transformed
span.quote: Data warping augmentations transform existing images such that their label is preserved. This encompasses augmentations such as geometric and color transformations, random erasing, adversarial training, and neural style transfer. Oversampling augmentations create synthetic instances and add them to the training set. This includes mixing images, feature space augmentations, and generative adversarial networks (GANs).

span.label: oversampling - a NEW instance is synthesised and added. The paper draws the distinction and then says in the next breath that it does not partition: GAN samples can be stacked with random cropping
span.quote: Oversampling and Data Warping augmentations do not form a mutually exclusive dichotomy. For example, GAN samples can be stacked with random cropping to further inflate the dataset.

span.label: data warping —distinct-from→ oversampling
span.note: holds when: the two are NOT mutually exclusive - GAN samples can be stacked with random cropping, so a single augmentation can be both · strength of the relation: 0.8
span.quote: Data warping augmentations transform existing images such that their label is preserved. This encompasses augmentations such as geometric and color transformations, random erasing, adversarial training, and neural style transfer. Oversampling augmentations create synthetic instances and add them to the training set. This includes mixing images, feature space augmentations, and generative adversarial networks (GANs). Oversampling and Data Warping augmentations do not form a mutually exclusive dichotomy. For example, GAN samples can be stacked with random cropping to further inflate the dataset.

span.label: Transfer Learning —distinct-from→ Pretraining
span.quote: This differs from Transfer Learning because in Transfer Learning, the network architecture such as VGG-16 [2] or ResNet [3] must be transferred as well as the weights.

span.label: Dropout —is-a→ regularization technique
span.quote: Dropout [7] is a regularization technique that zeros out the activation values of randomly chosen neurons during training. This constraint forces the network to learn more robust features rather than relying on the predictive capability of a small subset of neurons in the network.

span.label: Batch normalization —is-a→ regularization technique
span.quote: Batch normalization [9] is another regularization technique that normalizes the set of activations in a layer. Normalization works by subtracting the batch mean from each activation and dividing by the batch standard deviation.

span.label: Data Augmentation —causes→ overfitting
span.note: direction on the measure: reduces · the relation itself is separately evidenced · strength of the relation: 1
span.quote: Overfitting is generally not as much of an issue with access to big data. Data Augmentation prevents overfitting by modifying limited datasets to possess the characteristics of big data.

span.label: AlexNet used augmentation to expand its training set by three orders of magnitude and the authors credit it with more than a percentage point of error reduction
span.quote: Data Augmentation is used in their experiments to increase the dataset size by a magnitude of 2048.

span.label: GAN-based augmentation beat classic augmentation on liver lesion classification on both sensitivity and specificity
span.quote: This improved classification performance from 78.6% sensitivity and 88.4% specificity using classic augmentations to 85.7% sensitivity and 92.4% specificity using GAN-based Data Augmentation.

span.label: horizontal flipping is far commoner than vertical, and is not label-preserving on text recognition datasets
span.quote: Horizontal axis flipping is much more common than flipping the vertical axis.

span.label: converting to grayscale costs about three points of classification accuracy against RGB on ImageNet and PASCAL VOC
span.quote: Chatifled et al. [59] found a ~ 3% classification accuracy drop between grayscale and RGB images with their experiments on ImageNet [12] and the PASCAL [60] VOC dataset.

span.label: in a head-to-head comparison of geometric against photometric augmentation, cropping produced the most accurate classifier
span.quote: Their results find that the cropping geometric transformation results in the most accurate classifier The italic value denote high performance according to the comparative metrics Geometric versus photometric transformations Taylor and Nitschke [63] provide a comparative study on the effectiveness of geometric and photometric (color space) transformations.

span.label: randomly swapping pixels inside a small window lowered CIFAR-10 error against the same architecture without it
span.quote: Experimenting across different filter sizes and probabilities of shuffling the pixels at each step, they demonstrate the effectiveness of this by achieving a 5.66% error rate on CIFAR-10 compared to an error rate of 6.33% achieved without the use of PatchShuffle Regularization.

span.label: blurring is proposed to buy resistance to motion blur at test time and sharpening to capture more object detail - the augmentation chosen for the corruption expected
span.quote: Intuitively, blurring images for Data Augmentation could lead to higher resistance to motion blur during testing.

span.label: the safety of an augmentation defined as label preservation, with the cat/dog against 6/9 example
span.quote: The safety of a Data Augmentation method refers to its likelihood of preserving the label post-transformation.

span.label: the full list of augmentation families this survey covers
span.quote: The augmentations listed in this survey are geometric transformations, color space transformations, kernel filters, mixing images, random erasing, feature space augmentation, adversarial training, GAN-based augmentation, neural style transfer, and meta-learning schemes.

span.label: the factor by which AlexNet's augmentation multiplied the dataset, and the error reduction claimed for it
span.quote: Data Augmentation is used in their experiments to increase the dataset size by a magnitude of 2048.

span.label: sensitivity and specificity before and after GAN-based augmentation on liver lesion classification
span.quote: This improved classification performance from 78.6% sensitivity and 88.4% specificity using classic augmentations to 85.7% sensitivity and 92.4% specificity using GAN-based Data Augmentation.

span.label: the CIFAR-10 error rate with and without PatchShuffle regularization, and the hyperparameters that achieved it
span.quote: Experimenting across different filter sizes and probabilities of shuffling the pixels at each step, they demonstrate the effectiveness of this by achieving a 5.66% error rate on CIFAR-10 compared to an error rate of 6.33% achieved without the use of PatchShuffle Regularization.

span.label: the accuracy drop from grayscale against RGB
span.quote: Chatifled et al. [59] found a ~ 3% classification accuracy drop between grayscale and RGB images with their experiments on ImageNet [12] and the PASCAL [60] VOC dataset.

span.label: the rotation degree parameter, on which the safety of a rotation augmentation depends
span.quote: Rotation augmentations are done by rotating the image right or left on an axis between 1° and 359°.

p.note: The full text of this article is not redistributable, so it is not included here. Every tag above carries the exact sentence it was made from, quoted under fair quotation. The article itself is at https://doi.org/10.1186/s40537-019-0197-0.
